 Judgment

This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company, against the award dated 03.06.2024 passed in M.C.O.P.No.31 of 2017 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal/Subordinate Court, Mudukulathur on the issue of negligence and quantum.

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsels on either side and perused the relevant records.
3.

The case as set out in the claim petition is stated hereunder:
On 18.01.2016 at about 11.00 p.m., a private bus, that belongs to the first respondent bearing Registration No.TN-59- BC-0825, was proceeding along Melur main road.

When the bus was proceeding in front of Uthangudi Ponmani Garden apartment,
because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the _____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis bus(first respondent), the cleaner of the bus, who was travelling in the said bus, fell down from the bus.
Due to the said impact, the claimant, who is the cleaner of the bus, suffered fracture over his right leg and sustained injuries all over the body.

For the said act, the owner of the bus, namely,
the first respondent and the insurer of the said bus, namely, the second respondent,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

4. The said details were counteracted by the second respondent/insurance company by filing counter to the effect that while the claimant/cleaner was standing on the footboard of the bus, as the driver of the first respondent applied break, the claimant fell down and sustained injuries.

Thereby,
the claimant has contributed to the accident.
The claimant is put to strict proof of his age and income.
As the claimant contributed to the accident, the second respondent/claimant is not liable to pay compensation.
5. At trial, the claimant has been examined as P.W.1 and 21 documents were marked.

On the second respondent/insurance companys side, the Legal Manager of the second _____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent/Insurance Company, Mr.Saravanan was examined as R.W.1 and Dr.Arif Anwar has been examined as R.W.2 and three documents were marked.
Ex. R1
is the copy of the insurance policy.

Ex.C1 is the disability certificate issued by the Medical Board,
Ramnathapuram.

6. Upon consideration, the Tribunal has fixed contributory negligence to the extent of 10% on the claimant and directed the second respondent/insurance company to pay the compensation at Rs.12,32,850/- (90% of Rs.13,69,833/-) to the claimant.

7. The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal is given hereunder:

It appears that on the claimant side, the claimant alone has been examined as P.W.1 and no other ocular witness has been examined either by the claimant or by the appellant/second respondent/Insurance company.
9. As per the testimony of P.W.1, it is only because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the first respondent/bus, the accident has happened.

Therefore, for the accident occurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the abovesaid bus, the appellant/Insurance company,
who is the insurer, is liable to pay compensation.
In the given circumstances, fixing of 90% on the appellant/insurance company needs no interference.

10. As regards the quantum, the main grievance of the learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company is that for the partial permanent disability, by adopting multiplier method an amount of R s . 1 0 , 2 8 , 1 6 0 / - i s g r a n t e d b y t h e T r i b u n a l i s o n t h e
_ _ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis higher side.
11. From the evidence of P.W.1, it is pellucid that as the claimant fell down from the bus and the bus ran over his two legs, he sustained injuries.
From the treatment records, it appears that he sustained fracture over both the legs.

At the first instance, he was taken to the Government Rajaji Hospital,
Madurai and treated as an inpatient in I.C.U and thereafter, he was admitted at Meenakshi Mission Hospital, Madurai on 29.01.2016 and discharged on 25.02.2016.

He was admitted in the Meenskshi Mission Hospital for the problem of vascular repair in respect of the right thigh and leg with popliteal region, for which on 01.02.2016, wound debridement was done and on 08.02.2016, skin drafting was done.
He has undergone fasciotomy.
Thereafter, for the infected fasciotomy, he took treatment at Meenakshi Mission Hospital.
12. It is relevant to note about the effects of vascular repair with infected fasciotomy.
As per google search, the following are the effects of infected fasciotomy:

. Amputation rates in patients who develop SSI after fasciotomy are reported to be as high as 35%.

Sepsis: Infections can lead to sepsis, which can progress to widespread organ failure.
Death: Infections can lead to serious adverse outcomes including death.
Other complications of fasciotomy include:
Wound infection Osteomyelitis Scarring Delayed bone healing Pain and nerve injury Permanent muscle weakness
Chronic venous insufficiency Cosmetic problems

Factors that can increase the risk of surgical site infection (SSI) after fasciotomy include: Open fractures _____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis History of smoking Higher body mass index (BMI) Higher levels of neutrophil, glucose,
globulin, and total carbon dioxide Renal insufficiency 13.

Most specifically, viability of the limb may be affected, amputation rate is reported to be as high as 35% and the infections can lead to sepsis including death and other complications and the factors that will increase the risk of infection, have been mentioned supra.

The disability is assessed at 60%
by the Medical Board.
As the claimant was aged about 27 years and was working as cleaner in the first respondent/bus, his monthly income was fixed at Rs. 6,000/-.
For future prospects, 40% was added and his income was fixed at Rs.8,400/-.

By applying multiplier 17, for 60% of the disability,
an amount of Rs.10,28,160/- was granted under the head for partial permanent disability.
Based on the disability suffered by the injured, I dons find any good reason in computing the amount for partial permanent disability.
The amounts awarded under the other heads appear to be reasonable and acceptable and need no interference.

In the result,
(i) The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed without being admitted.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

(ii) The appellant/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation awarded by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.12,32,850/- (less the amount already deposited if any) to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.31 of 2017 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal/Sub Court, Mudukulathur,
within a period of eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
